conventions.dates: Gregorian calendar. start/end are inclusive calendar dates, not UTC instants. Year envelopes and upper bounds are not asserted event days.
conventions.places: Named historical locations checked against sources. geometry is null until independently geocoded; no present-day museum or headquarters is substituted for an event location.
conventions.interpretation: MMS connections identify the supplied v37 narrative; they are separate from the historical claims and do not assign automatic wave scores.
conventions.selection: Purposive research anchors expanding people, works, movements and events named in MMS v37. Not every dated occurrence is explicitly listed in MMS; this is not an exhaustive or representative sample.

events.title: Thoreau begins living at Walden Pond

time.note: Move-in date, not publication of Walden or the start of Transcendentalism.

places.name: Thoreau's cabin site, Walden Pond, Concord, Massachusetts, USA

events.historicalSummary: Thoreau began occupying the house he built near Walden Pond.

mms.connection: Concrete place/time anchor for the Romantic Epoch's Transcendentalist theme; the event is in 1845, not reassigned to the 1842 marker.

openQuestions: Geocode the historical cabin site rather than the visitor-centre replica.

events.title: Proclamation of the Paris Commune

time.note: Proclamation after the elections; distinct from the March 18 uprising.

places.name: Hôtel de Ville and its square, Paris, France

events.historicalSummary: The elected Commune was publicly proclaimed at the Hôtel de Ville.

mms.connection: Commune Epoch: civic experimentation. Suppression should be a separate event or interval, not merged with the proclamation.

openQuestions: Add the uprising and Bloody Week as distinct records; geocode the square.

events.title: Construction begins at Wardenclyffe

time.note: Envelope for a year-only start date. The institutional history does not establish an exact groundbreaking day.

places.name: Wardenclyffe laboratory and tower site, Shoreham, Long Island, New York, USA

events.historicalSummary: Construction began on Tesla's planned wireless communication and power-transfer facility.

mms.connection: Tesla Epoch's principal geographic technology anchor.

openQuestions: Resolve any more precise start date using construction records; distinguish laboratory construction, tower construction, experiments and later demolition.

events.title: Wright brothers' successful powered flights

time.note: Four flights that day; a time-of-day is not asserted here.

places.name: 1903 flight grounds, Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina, USA

events.historicalSummary: Orville and Wilbur Wright made successful controlled, powered flights at Kill Devil Hills.

mms.connection: Innovation surrounding the Tesla Epoch; retains the actual 1903 date.

openQuestions: Geocode the flight grounds/launch marker, not the hilltop monument or the town centre of Kitty Hawk.

events.title: Battle of Verdun

time.note: Conventional battle interval, not a single event day.

places.name: Battlefield north of Verdun, Meuse, France

events.historicalSummary: A prolonged battle took place on the heights north of Verdun.

mms.connection: WWI trough example; destruction/institutional counter-pressure in the MMS reading.

openQuestions: Use a battlefield footprint or named sub-battles; a museum pin would not represent the whole battle.

events.title: Somme offensive

time.note: Series of battles; preserve the duration rather than substituting July 1 for the whole offensive.

events.historicalSummary: The Somme offensive comprised a series of battles along the Somme Valley.

mms.connection: A second geographically distinct WWI trough example.

openQuestions: Source an appropriate battlefield footprint and distinguish opening-day actions from the wider campaign.

events.title: Creation of The Persistence of Memory

time.note: Catalogue dates the work 1931 and lists it in the June 3–15 exhibition. June 15 is a conservative inferred upper bound from that exhibition, not an asserted painting day; the individual display start is not established.

events.historicalSummary: Dalí's painting is dated 1931. The checked catalogue does not establish its creation site or exact creation day.

mms.connection: Defining Surrealist Epoch artwork. Do not move the wave's provisional July 1 calibration automatically on the basis of an exhibition date.

openQuestions: Locate a reliable primary account of where it was painted and when. MoMA's current custody is not its creation location; a depicted landscape is not proof of studio location.

events.title: The Persistence of Memory in Dalí's Pierre Colle exhibition

time.note: Exhibition dates in the Foundation catalogue, entry 23; not creation dates.

events.historicalSummary: The Foundation lists the painting in the June 1931 Dalí exhibition at Pierre Colle in Paris.

mms.connection: A public-presentation anchor associated with the defining artwork, separate from the act of painting.

openQuestions: Verify the gallery's 1931 street address before placing a precise map pin.

events.title: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima

time.note: Minute-level historical time, not a second-accurate timestamp.

events.historicalSummary: An atomic bomb devastated Hiroshima on August 6, 1945, at about 08:15 local time.

mms.connection: Event discussed in the postwar trough narrative; it occurred in 1945, not 1946.

openQuestions: If a hypocentre pin is needed, source it separately and distinguish it from the affected area.

events.title: Atomic bombing of Nagasaki

time.note: Minute-level historical time, not a second-accurate timestamp.

events.historicalSummary: An atomic bomb exploded over Nagasaki on August 9, 1945, at about 11:02 local time.

mms.connection: Separate place/time record within the postwar trough narrative; actual event year is 1945.

openQuestions: Source the hypocentre and/or affected-area geometry separately from museum location.

events.title: The Beatles' first Cavern Club performance

time.note: A concrete early performance; not a universal date when the band became famous or ceased being underground.

places.name: Original Cavern Club, Liverpool, England, United Kingdom

events.historicalSummary: The Beatles first performed at the Cavern Club on February 9, 1961.

mms.connection: Specific early-band activity for the Beat Epoch's music theme; does not equate the Beatles with the Beat literary movement.

openQuestions: Check the original venue footprint rather than assuming the present reconstructed club is identical.

events.title: Gagarin launches aboard Vostok 1

time.note: Launch time; the full spaceflight occupies a longer interval and route.

places.name: Baikonur Cosmodrome, Site No. 1, Kazakhstan (then USSR)

events.historicalSummary: Vostok 1 launched with Yuri Gagarin, who became the first human in space.
openQuestions: Geocode Site No. 1. A launch pin represents departure, not the entire orbital path or landing.

events.title: Dalí's reported cosmogonic experience at Perpignan station

time.note: Date attributed to Dalí's reported experience in the municipal account; not the date of the later painting or public reception.

events.historicalSummary: Perpignan's municipal history dates Dalí's account of a cosmogonic experience at the station to September 19, 1963.

mms.connection: Place-linked visionary experience discussed in the Hyperborean Corridor narrative.

openQuestions: Consult the cited autobiographical account for a direct first-person source; distinguish this from his August 27, 1965 reception and the later painting.

events.title: Nevermind recording sessions in Southern California

time.note: Specialist sessionography's combined session interval; not a verified day-by-day allocation between the two studios or every track on the album.

places.name: Sound City Studios, Van Nuys, California, USA

events.historicalSummary: The specialist sessionography groups Sound City and Devonshire work into a May 2–28, 1991 session period.

mms.connection: Grunge Epoch's defining album: creative production is geographically distinct from public release.

openQuestions: Corroborate finer session dates with studio logs or participant accounts. Do not label all tracks as first conceived or fully recorded here.

events.title: Release of Nevermind

time.note: Official artist timeline's release date; regional release differences may require additional records.

events.historicalSummary: Nirvana's official timeline dates Nevermind's release to September 24, 1991.

mms.connection: Public-release anchor for the Grunge Epoch. Chart impact and recording are distinct events.

openQuestions: A distributed commercial release has no single verified event site here. Do not substitute Seattle, a studio, or a label headquarters without defining a separate local event.
